usdRate.sourceName: National Bank of Georgia official exchange rate (USD)
usdRate.note: GEL 2.5992 per US dollar, set on 30 October 2026 and valid from 31 October 2026; World Bank 2025 average 2.743.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: National Statistics Office of Georgia (Geostat), Inflation Rate in Georgia, October 2026
inflation_cpi.note: Annual CPI inflation 5.9% in October 2026 (5.6% in September; core 4.0%), published 3 November 2026. World Bank 2025 average 3.9%.

inflation_projection.sourceName: National Bank of Georgia 3% inflation target; CPI 5.9% (Oct 2026, Geostat), 3.9% in 2025 (World Bank)
inflation_projection.note: Inflation has averaged well above the 3% target over the last five years (including 10-12% in 2021-22), so 4.5% is used for planning.

policy_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics (National Bank of Georgia refinancing rate)
policy_rate.note: Monetary policy rate held at 8.25% on 21 October 2026; next decision 16 December 2026. Secondary source because nbg.gov.ge loads its rate by script.

savings_account_rate.sourceName: National Bank of Georgia, effective interest rates on deposits (bank comparison table)
savings_account_rate.note: Median effective rate on GEL demand deposits (daily balance) among banks that list one, about 5%; the two largest banks' demand entries are not usable, and USD demand deposits pay about 0.5-1%. Table date not shown; read 31 October 2026.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: National Bank of Georgia, effective interest rates on deposits (bank comparison table)
fdr_3m_rate.note: Average effective rate on 3-month GEL term deposits at the two largest banks (8.40% and 8.83%); other banks 6.1-9.7%; USD 3-month deposits pay 1-2.6%.

fdr_1y_rate.sourceName: National Bank of Georgia, effective interest rates on deposits (bank comparison table)
fdr_1y_rate.note: Average effective rate on 12-month GEL term deposits at the two largest banks (8.85% and 9.25%); other banks 8-10.2%; USD 12-month deposits pay 1.4-4%.

dps_rate.note: Banks offer accumulative savings deposits with regular top-ups, but the NBG comparison table does not list them and no published rate was found.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: Trading Economics (IMF), Georgia deposit interest rate
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Average rate paid by commercial banks on deposits, August 2026 (9.30% in July); secondary source citing the IMF; World Bank FR.INR.DPST 2025 average 10.6%.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or dedicated retail savings bond for individuals was found; treasury notes and bonds are auctioned by the Ministry of Finance mainly to banks.

tbill_91d_rate.note: Ministry of Finance treasury bill auctions (maturities up to one year) are published on mof.ge and nbg.gov.ge, but the result pages load by script and no yield could be read; a 91-day bill may not be issued.

tbond_5y_rate.note: 5-year treasury note yields appear in Ministry of Finance auction results and the NBG GEL yield curve, but both pages load by script and no figure could be read; Trading Economics shows no Georgia bond yield.

tbond_10y_rate.note: 10-year treasury bond yields appear in Ministry of Finance auction results, but the pages load by script and no figure could be read.

tax_bank_interest.note: Interest paid to an individual is taxed at source at 5% and is then final: it is not included in gross income or taxed further (Article 131(1) and (3)).

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate exists; interest on government debt securities and NBG securities held by individuals is exempt from income tax.

deposit_insurance_limit.note: Georgia has a deposit insurance scheme (Deposit Insurance Agency), but dia.ge refused the connection and no other official page stating the current limit per depositor could be read.

credit_card_rate_cap.note: No page stating a legal interest-rate cap or a typical credit card rate could be read; NBG loan-rate statistics load by script.

equity_return_low.sourceName: No meaningful local stock market (Trading Economics tracks no Georgian index); global equities in GEL; after-tax 1-year GEL deposit 9.05% less 5% = 8.6%
equity_return_low.note: Low case: global shares earn about 4% in dollars and the lari stays stable, well below safe lari deposits.

equity_return_base.sourceName: Global equity long-run return about 7% in USD; GEL per USD 2.60 (NBG); inflation gap with the US about 2 points
equity_return_base.note: The Georgian Stock Exchange is tiny and illiquid, so the base is a global index fund in lari: about 7% in dollars plus about 2% a year of expected lari depreciation, within 4 points of the after-tax deposit rate.

equity_return_high.sourceName: Global equity long-run returns; lari depreciation of 2005-2025
equity_return_high.note: High case: strong global equity returns plus faster lari depreciation.

gold_return_low.sourceName: Gold USD 3,876/oz on 30 Oct 2026, 31% below the January 2026 high (Trading Economics)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: gold barely keeps up after the 2025-26 spike and the lari stays stable.

gold_return_base.sourceName: Gold price history (Trading Economics); NBG 3% target vs 2% US inflation
gold_return_base.note: Base case: dollar gold rises about 4% a year and the lari loses about 2% a year against the dollar.

gold_return_high.note: High case: a repeat of gold's strong 2005-2025 trend plus lari depreciation.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: NBG policy rate 8.25%; GEL deposit rates (NBG comparison table)
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: deposit rates fall as inflation returns to the 3% target, giving about 6.5% after tax.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: 12-month GEL deposits 9.05% less 5% tax = 8.6% (NBG comparison table)
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case: a little below today's after-tax 1-year lari deposit rate, allowing for some easing.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Highest 12-month GEL deposit rates 9.6-10.2% (NBG comparison table) less 5% tax
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case: rates stay high and savers use the better-paying banks or tax-free treasury securities.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: The Insurance State Supervision Service publishes market statistics but no life claim settlement ratio could be found.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold mainly as credit-linked or group cover; no published premium table per GEL 1,000 of cover by age was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: The Universal Healthcare Programme pays part of hospital costs with patient co-payments; no official figure for a typical out-of-pocket cost of a major private hospital stay was found.

health_premium_table.note: Private health insurance is sold as fixed packages, not per sum insured, and no published premium table per GEL 100,000 of cover was found.

oop_health_share.note: Latest World Bank figure is for 2023 (older than 2025).

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: Geostat: health prices up 8.4% year on year in October 2026 (out-patient services 11.7%); out-of-pocket share of health spending 59% (World Bank)
goal_inflation_health.note: Medicine and private care are mostly paid out of pocket and health prices are rising faster than headline inflation, but 8.4% reflects the current spike, so 6% is used for the long run.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: Geostat October 2026: school education prices up 6.6-8.8% year on year, tertiary down 32.9%; planning inflation 4.5%
goal_inflation_education.note: Pre-primary, primary and secondary fees are rising well above headline inflation while the tertiary fall reflects a one-off policy change, so 6% is used.

life_expectancy.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_expectancy.note: Men 70.1, women 79.5 (UN WPP estimate for 2026); World Bank 2024 figure 74.7.

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects via georank.org
life_table_remaining.note: Remaining years computed from georank's expected age at death by current age (UN WPP 2026 estimate, mid-year).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 25.2 (2025, World Bank), 29.2 (2040) and 39.5 (2065, populationpyramid.net/georgia/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Trading Economics (Social Service Agency of Georgia), retirement age men and women
retirement_age_default.note: State pension age 65 for men and 60 for women (Trading Economics citing the Social Service Agency, 2026); the Funded Pension Law (Art. 2(q)) uses the same age, defined by the Law on State Pensions.

retirement_age_government.note: No official page stating the retirement or age limit for public servants could be read; the state pension age (65 men, 60 women) applies to all.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: NBG policy rate 8.25%; GEL deposit rates (NBG comparison table)
retirement_return_low.note: Low case: lari deposit rates fall toward 6-7% as inflation settles.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: 12-month GEL deposits 9.05% less 5% tax = 8.6% (NBG comparison table)
retirement_return_base.note: Base case capped below the after-tax 1-year lari deposit rate.

retirement_return_high.note: High case: today's after-tax 1-year deposit rate holds for the long run.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: After-tax GEL deposits 8.6%; global equity low case 5%
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced mix if global shares lag and deposit rates fall.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: After-tax GEL deposits 8.6%; global equity in GEL 9%
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case: roughly half lari deposits and half global shares in lari terms.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: After-tax GEL deposits 8.6%; global equity high case 12%
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case for a growth-leaning mix.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: Georgia pays a flat non-contributory state pension, but the Social Service Agency, Ministry of Health and Ministry of Finance pages refused automated access and no source stating the 2026 amount could be read.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Georgia pays a flat state pension from age 65 (men) and 60 (women) (Trading Economics citing the Social Service Agency), but no readable source confirmed whether it is means-tested or its residence conditions: the Social Service Agency and Ministry of Health sites refused automated access.

gratuity_rule.note: No statutory gratuity or end-of-service payment per year of service was found; the Labour Code text could not be read to confirm severance rules on dismissal.

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Law of Georgia on Funded Pension (matsne.gov.ge); retirement ages via Trading Economics
public_pension_scheme.note: Mandatory funded pension (Pension Agency) since 2019 for employees: 2% of salary from the employee, 2% from the employer and 2% from the state (1% on income GEL 24,000-60,000, none above) (Art. 3(6)); savings can be drawn at the state pension age (Art. 2(q), 24), 65 for men and 60 for women; returns depend on investment, so payouts are not inflation-linked. Employees aged 40+ at launch could opt out (Art. 22).

savings_account.note: Offered in lari and in US dollars or euros; foreign-currency deposits pay much less.

dps.note: Deposit with regular top-ups; terms vary by bank.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate for individuals; interest on government securities is tax-exempt for individuals.

tbill_91d.note: Discount bills with maturities up to one year, auctioned by the Ministry of Finance through the NBG mainly to banks.

equity_fund.note: Few domestic funds; residents mainly reach diversified index funds abroad through brokerage accounts.

insuranceRegulator.name: Insurance State Supervision Service of Georgia

insuranceComplaints.name: Insurance State Supervision Service of Georgia, consumer page
insuranceComplaints.note: The regulator handles consumer questions about insurers; disputes go to the courts.
